notes: Cresud SACIF y A (NASDAQ: CRESY; BCBA: CRES) — leading Argentine agricultural company holding ~590,000 hectares (~1.46M acres) of productive farmland across Argentina, Bolivia, Paraguay, and (via 33% stake in BrasilAgro / AGRO3.SA) Brazil. Also owns ~53.7% of IRSA, the largest Argentine real-estate company (shopping centers, offices). Reports in inflation-adjusted ARS under IAS 29 (Argentina is a hyperinflationary economy); files 20-F with SEC in USD using year-end FX. Fiscal year ends June 30. Five operating segments: Agricultural Business (own farms — crops, beef, dairy, sugarcane), Real Estate Argentina (IRSA), Real Estate International, BrasilAgro (consolidated subsidiary), and Other. Figures here are USD-converted from 20-F filings (CIK 1034957). Argentine peso devaluation distorts year-over-year comparability — USD figures are the cleanest cut. Net debt is consolidated (includes IRSA + BrasilAgro debt, much of which is non-recourse to Cresud parent).

periods.notes: FY20: revenue ~US$590M. COVID year + Argentine peso collapse. Heavy losses driven by IRSA real-estate impairments. Drought in late season.
FY21: ag prices rallying (corn, soy, beef). Revenue ~US$720M. EBITDA recovery to ~US$130M. Debt reduction via farm sales.
FY22: peak commodity-price year (Russia/Ukraine). Revenue US$1.0B+. EBITDA US$200M (record). Strong sugarcane crush at BrasilAgro; cattle realization.
FY23: severe Argentine drought hit own-farm crop yields. Revenue US$1.1B but EBITDA compressed to ~US$130M. BrasilAgro carried results. Massive ARS devaluation in late FY (Milei election).

FY24 (20-F filed Oct 2024): revenue ~US$1.23B. Recovery from drought. Adj EBITDA ~US$175M. Net debt down to ~US$785M after farm sales + IRSA dividend distribution. Argentine economy stabilizing under Milei. Strong real-estate (IRSA) contribution. EPS ~US$0.65 per ADR.
